**Visual analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Root system and crown region of a cereal plant (wheat/grass), photographed against a blue sky
- **Key features**:
  - Roots are pale cream/yellowish-white with a somewhat fuzzy texture
  - Dark brown-to-black discoloration at the crown/stem base
  - Necrotic brown tips on multiple roots
  - Roots appear thin and somewhat stunted
  - Some roots show rotting/decay progression from tip toward crown

**Reasoning through classes:**

The image shows the root and crown of a cereal seedling with classic symptoms of root rot/damping-off:
- The dark discoloration at the soil line (crown) and rotting root tips are hallmark signs
- **Rhizoctonia Damping-Off** (*Rhizoctonia solani*) causes: browning of the subcrown internode and crown, root tip necrosis, and general root rot in cereal seedlings — precisely what's visible here
- Other root diseases in the list don't match: Eyespot causes stem-base lesions (not root tip necrosis), Cephalosporium Stripe and Dwarf Bunt affect leaves/heads, all the rust/mildew classes affect aerial parts
- The brown-black crown discoloration combined with necrotic root tips is textbook Rhizoctonia root rot/damping-off

This pattern — root tip necrosis progressing upward with dark crown browning — is characteristic of Rhizoctonia solani damping-off/root rot in wheat or barley. No aerial symptoms (rust, mildew, streaks) are visible; the pathology is confined to the root and crown tissue."}
